doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Joining the Saturday Night Live band
summary: Parker weighed the weekly commitment before joining the SNL band after years of guest shots, and mentions guest artists without bands.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It’s a terrific answer. Thank you. When you got the call to play in the Saturday Night Live band was it a no-brainer to take it or was there something about committing every Saturday that gave you pause?

I considered it carefully because I was pretty busy at the time and they did say what are your weekends like. And I weighed the pros and cons about it and decided to take it because I hadn’t done it before. I had done guest shots on the show since the early 70s. You know I played with a guest artist on the show, which is relatively easy. I mean you rehearse with the artist during the week somewhere and then you come Saturday morning or Saturday afternoon and rehearse again in the studio and camera blocking and all that stuff. Then there’s a dress rehearsal, then you perform with the artist. So it was pretty easy. And I did enjoy that. So when they asked me to join the band I said okay I’ll do it. And it got to the point where I was turning down things. Not just record dates but other tours and things that I said eh — I wish I could have done that, that would have been great. But you do commit to not only Saturday but usually a couple of other days during the week where you do pre-records. And nowadays the musical artist usually brings their own band, but in the 70s and 80s you know there were a lot of people like Leo Sayer or Eric Clapton or Elvis Costello or Linda Ronstadt, Aaron Neville, where they didn’t have a band so they used a put together band from New York or they used certain members of the Saturday Night band itself to do their performance. And it was always two tunes. Now it’s — I don’t know if they still do two tunes or not. I haven’t watched the show in a while. But yeah, it’s a commitment. And God bless — Shawn Pelton’s been doing it ever since I stopped you know. He’s been there since ’92 so it’s thirty years.
